ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of circle $O$, with C and D being two points on the circle. $OC \parallel BD$, and $OC$ intersects $AD$ at point E. $AC = CD$; if $OE = 2$ and $AD = 8$, find the radius of circle $O$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From (1) we know that $OC\perp AD$,\\
$\because AD=8$,\\
$\therefore AE=\frac{1}{2}AD=4$,\\
$\because OE=2$,\\
$\therefore OA=\sqrt{OE^{2}+AE^{2}}=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ the radius of circle $O$ is $\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, AB is the horizontal diameter, and O is on AB; C and D are located on the upper arc of the circle; BD is the chord from D to B, OC is the line segment from the center O of the circle to C, and in the figure OC is parallel to BD; AD is the chord from A to D, and intersects OC at E; AC and CD are also drawn, and the problem gives AC = CD. Then reason: Because AB is the diameter of circle O, and D is on the circle, according to the fact that the inscribed angle subtended by a diameter is a right angle, ∠ADB = 90°, that is, AD ⟂ BD. Also because OC ∥ BD, AD ⟂ OC. Point E is at the intersection of AD and OC, therefore AE ⟂ OE, and triangle AEO is a right triangle. At the same time, C, E, O are collinear, and OC ⟂ AD, so CE is the altitude in triangle ACD drawn from C to AD. Because AC = CD, triangle ACD is an isosceles triangle with C as the vertex and AD as the base; the altitude to the base of an isosceles triangle is also a median, so E is the midpoint of AD. Given AD = 8, therefore AE = AD/2 = 4. Given OE = 2, in right triangle AEO, by the Pythagorean theorem, OA = sqrt(AE^2 + OE^2) = sqrt(4^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(20) = 2sqrt(5). OA is the radius of circle O, so the radius is 2sqrt(5).
